sections.description: This section outlines the patient's demographic profile, past medical history, the trigger exposure to semaglutide, the sequence of acute symptoms leading to hospitalization, the evolution of neuromuscular complaints over four months, and the initial physical exam and laboratory findings that prompted further investigation.
subtopics: Patient age, sex, comorbidities (obesity, NAFLD, hypertension, hypothyroidism)
Indication for semaglutide initiation and dosing regimen
Acute gastrointestinal reaction within hours after first semaglutide dose
Hospitalization for nausea/vomiting, dehydration‑related acute renal failure and metabolic acidosis
Initial CK level (337 U/L) and lack of classic rhabdomyolysis signs
Development of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation during acute admission
Deconditioning after discharge and progressive proximal weakness over four months
Onset of dysphagia and dysphonia leading to re‑presentation
Physical examination findings at tertiary center (proximal muscle weakness without rash or systemic signs)
Trend of CK elevation from baseline to peak (~3992 U/L)

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology and Differential Diagnosis of Necrotising Myopathies
sections.description: Provides a focused review of immune‑mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM), its serologic markers and seronegative forms, drug‑induced necrotising myopathies including statins and GLP‑1 receptor agonists, and how to differentiate IMNM from acute toxic rhabdomyolysis on clinical and histologic grounds.
subtopics: Definition of IMNM and key clinical hallmarks (proximal weakness, CK elevation)
Autoantibody associations: anti‑HMGCR and anti‑SRP; prevalence of seronegative IMNM
Mechanisms of drug‑induced necrotising myopathy (immune activation vs direct toxicity)
GLP‑1 receptor agonist effects on skeletal muscle mass and reported rhabdomyolysis cases
Pathophysiologic differences between rhabdomyolysis (rapid CK rise/fall) and IMNM (sustained CK elevation)
"Membrane attack complex" deposition on muscle fibers as an immunologic marker
Potential role of pre‑existing subclinical autoimmunity (e.g., isolated SS‑B positivity)
Key features differentiating polymyositis/dermatomyositis from IMNM

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Work‑up and Clinical Reasoning in This Case
sections.description: Details the systematic diagnostic approach employed—including laboratory panels, imaging studies, tissue biopsy—and explains how each test contributed to confirming IMNM while excluding alternative etiologies.
subtopics: Comprehensive CK kinetics correlated with symptom timeline
"Transaminase vs muscle" interpretation: AST/ALT elevations in context of CK levels
Autoimmune serology panel results (negative ANA panel, negative HMGCR/SRP antibodies) and significance
Low‑titer SS‑B positivity: interpretation in the absence of ANA or SS‑A antibodies
MRI findings: symmetric proximal thigh edema suggesting inflammatory myopathy
Cardiac evaluation: echocardiogram & cardiac MRI findings suggestive/against myocarditis
Thoracic CT ruling out interstitial lung disease associated with connective tissue disease
Liver imaging & biopsies confirming NAFLD as chronic background unrelated to acute myopathy
"Gold standard" muscle biopsy findings: necrotic/regenerating fibers, CD68+ macrophages, MAC deposition, sparse CD3+ T cells
Application of WHO–Uppsala Monitoring Centre causality criteria to assess drug relationship

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Management Strategies for Immune‑Mediated Necrotising Myopathy
sections.description: Reviews evidence‑based treatment modalities for IMNM with emphasis on drug‑induced cases—rationale for high‐dose steroids, intravenous immunoglobulin administration, tapering protocols—and outlines supportive care measures taken during the patient’s hospital course.
[subtopics]: "Immediate" steps: discontinuation of semaglutide and aggressive intravenous hydration
"Corticosteroid regimen": IV methylprednisolone 1000 mg daily ×5 days followed by oral prednisone 1 mg/kg daily taper schedule
"IVIG protocol": total dose 2 g/kg divided over four days; indications for use in refractory weakness
"Monitoring therapeutic response": serial CK measurements, functional motor assessments
"Management of complications": treatment course for septic shock secondary to pseudomonal UTI during early taper
"Duration of immunosuppression": criteria for weaning off steroids after CK normalization
"Adjunctive considerations": physical therapy rehabilitation plans and nutritional support

sections.section_title: Outcome, Clinical Significance, and Future Directions
sections.description: Summarizes the patient’s long‐term recovery trajectory, highlights key lessons for clinicians regarding GLP‑1 receptor agonist safety monitoring, discusses pharmacovigilance implications and outlines research gaps that need addressing.
subtopics: Timeline of functional recovery and CK normalization up to ten months post‐diagnosis
Resolution of cardiac MRI abnormalities and cessation of atrial fibrillation episodes
"Off‐therapy" status: sustained remission without ongoing immunosuppression or repeat IVIG
"Implications for prescribing": risk assessment before initiating GLP‑1 RAs in patients with predisposing factors
"Pharmacovigilance": importance of reporting rare autoimmune adverse events associated with newer agents
"Causality considerations": strengths/limitations of single case evidence; ethical concerns about rechallenge
"Research priorities": mechanistic studies on GLP‑1 mediated immune activation; identification of genetic or serologic risk markers
"Broader clinical lesson": need for early neuromuscular evaluation when unexplained CK rise follows new medication exposure
